title: Rifleman (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
3.     MOS 0311, Rifleman (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. The Rifleman employs the M4 Service Rifle, the M320 Grenade
Launcher, the M3E1 multi-purpose anti-armor anti-personnel weapons system
(MAAWS), and the M27 Infantry Automatic Rifle (IAR). Riflemen are the
primary scouts, assault, and close combat forces available to the MAGTF.
They are the foundation of the marine infantry organization, and as such are
the nucleus of the fire team in the rifle squad, the scout team in the LAR
squad, and scout platoons in the infantry battalion. Noncommissioned
officers are assigned as fire team leaders, scout team leaders, and rifle
squad leaders.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must have a WS-B water survival.

             (2) Must possess a CL score of 90 or GT score of 90 or higher.



                                              3-22                    Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.

        (4) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF
assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit
training.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Infantry Marine Course (M03RG34) SOI Camp Lejeune,
NC or (M10RG32) SOI Camp Pendleton, CA.

        (2) Team leaders will complete the Advanced Infantry Marine Course
(M10M3X2) SOI, Camp Pendleton, CA, or (M03M3X4) SOI, Camp Lejeune, NC, or
(M21M3X1) DET HI, MCB HI, HI.

        (3) Squad leaders will complete the Infantry Small Unit Leaders
Course (M100302) SOI Camp Pendleton, CA, or (M030304) SOI Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (e), Infantry Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Infantry 55-3016.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Machine Gunner, 0331.
common_text: In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

They are the foundation of the marine infantry organization, and as such are the nucleus of the fire team in the rifle squad, the scout team in the LAR squad, and scout platoons in the infantry battalion. Noncommissioned officers are assigned as fire team leaders, scout team leaders, and rifle squad leaders. b. Prerequisites (1) Must have a WS-B water survival. (2) Must possess a CL score of 90 or GT score of 90 or higher. (3) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training. (4) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit training. c. Requirements (1) Complete the Infantry Marine Course (M03RG34) SOI Camp Lejeune, NC or (M10RG32) SOI Camp Pendleton, CA. nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
